title: Threat Detection Library - RHEL Privileged Action Validation Entry
description: Schema for a single entry in data/rhel-privileged-action-validations.json. Unlike this library's fourteen detection catalogues, a validation entry is not a production detection rule -- its 'search' field is a one-shot presence check ('did the expected event show up'), and its distinguishing fields (safe_test, test_step, rollback_step, test_result) describe executing an action once in a lab and confirming the telemetry/detection fired, not detecting the action in production traffic. See docs/validations.md for the full rationale and how this differs from a detection catalogue entry.

id.description: Stable catalogue identifier, sourced from the original workbook's Event ID column.

platform.description: Platform(s) this validation applies to, matching the platform enum convention used by data/redhat-detections.json. Every entry in this catalogue is RHEL-scoped today; the enum is deliberately narrow and should be widened only when a validation catalogue for another platform is added.

category.description: Original test grouping, e.g. User, Sudo, Service.

event_type.description: High-level privileged activity taxonomy, e.g. Account management, SELinux, Service management.

title.description: Canonical description of the privileged action.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the action (the workbook's Examples column).

typical_mechanism.description: Common command, API, syscall, or configuration mechanism.

mitre_attack.description: Resolved against the live MITRE ATT&CK STIX corpus at conversion time -- not copied verbatim from the workbook's ATT&CK Tactic column, which still used the pre-split 'Defense Evasion' tactic name MITRE has since divided into Stealth/Defense Impairment. A minority of entries (those with no technique to anchor a lookup) may have an empty tactics/techniques array rather than a guessed mapping.

note.description: Optional context note from the source workbook, e.g. 'context dependent' or 'when introducing software'.

primary_telemetry.description: Primary Linux/RHEL telemetry expected to record the action.

safe_test.description: Whether this action is suitable for controlled testing without intentional disruptive impact.

test_step.description: Command or action used to generate the event.

test_result.description: Pass/Fail/Partial/Not Tested tracking field -- set by whoever actually runs the validation, not by this library.

audit_key.description: Recommended/expected auditd key used to identify the activity.

audit_record_types.description: Expected correlated Linux audit record types.

expected_fields.description: Minimum fields useful for validation and detection.

validation_spl.description: Starter SPL to validate event presence in Splunk -- a presence check, not a tuned detection rule.
